edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS. (a) Base Salary. The Company shall pay the Executive an annual base salary of USD 450,000 (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to applicable deductions and withholdings. The Base Salary will be reviewed at least annually and may be increased, but not decreased, except with the Executive’s written consent. (b) Incentive Compensation. The Executive will be eligible to participate in any annual incentive program generally applicable to senior executives, subject to its terms and the applicable performance criteria established in writing. (c) Benefits. The Executive may participate in the health, dental, vision, retirement, paid-time-off, and other benefit plans the Company makes generally available to similarly situated executives, subject to the terms of those plans as amended from time to time. The Company will reimburse reasonable business expenses properly documented under its policies.
edits.name: 2. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE; TERMINATION. (a) Severance Amount. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay severance equal to twelve months of Base Salary in effect immediately before termination (the “Severance Amount”), in substantially equal installments over twelve months in accordance with regular payroll practices, subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims. The Company shall also pay any earned but unpaid Base Salary, accrued and unused paid time off to the extent required by applicable law, and properly documented unreimbursed business expenses. (b) Benefits Following Termination. Following a termination qualifying under subsection (a), the Executive may elect continuation coverage under applicable law at the Executive’s expense; the Company will pay the employer portion of the premium for twelve months, or until the Executive becomes eligible for comparable coverage through another employer, if earlier, to the extent permitted by law and the applicable plan. (c) Cause. “Cause” means: (i) the Executive’s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony involving fraud, dishonesty, or moral turpitude; (ii) the Executive’s willful and material misconduct in performing duties that causes material harm to the Company; (iii) the Executive’s material breach of this Agreement or a material written Company policy, which, if capable of cure, remains uncured for thirty days after written notice specifying the breach; or (iv) the Executive’s willful and continued failure to perform material duties after written notice and a reasonable opportunity of at least thirty days to cure. No act or omission is willful unless undertaken in bad faith or without a reasonable belief that it was in the Company’s best interests. (d) Good Reason. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent: a material reduction in Base Salary; a material diminution in duties, authority, or responsibilities; or a required relocation of the Executive’s principal work location by more than fifty miles. The Executive must give written notice within ninety days after the condition first occurs, allow the Company thirty days to cure, and resign within thirty days after the cure period expires if uncured. (e) Other Terminations. Either party may terminate employment at any time by written notice. The Company may terminate for Cause, and the Executive may resign without Good Reason. Upon any termination, the Company shall pay accrued compensation and other amounts required by law and the terms of applicable benefit plans. Nothing in this Agreement limits either party’s rights or obligations under applicable law.
edits.name: 3. SEVERANCE; TERMINATION

edits.text: 4. LIMITED NON-COMPETITION. During employment and for twelve months after termination for any reason, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, perform for or provide services to a competitor specifically named in Schedule A, but only in a role involving activities that are the same as or substantially similar to the material activities the Executive performed or supervised for the Company during the twelve months before termination and only with respect to products or services with which the Executive was materially involved. Schedule A must be completed and agreed in writing by both parties before execution of this Agreement; no entity not listed in the executed Schedule A is a competitor for purposes of this Section. The restriction does not prohibit passive ownership of up to two percent of a publicly traded company, work in a noncompetitive business unit, or activities that do not involve competitive products or services. During the post-termination restricted period, the Company shall continue to pay the Executive the Base Salary in effect at termination, in regular payroll installments, and continue the employer-paid benefits described in Section 3(b), subject to applicable law and plan terms. The Company may waive the restriction by written notice, in which case its obligations to provide post-termination compensation under this Section shall cease as of the effective date of the waiver. The parties intend this Section to be enforced only to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.
edits.name: 4. LIMITED NON-COMPETITION
